evidence: Parsed all five frozen judge.toml files with tomllib. Types by suite: gates/render 1 binary and gates/constraints 2 binary (all_pass; render/judge.toml:20, constraints/judge.toml:20,29); scored/functional 42 binary, weights 1.0/1.5/2.0 (weighted_mean); scored/polish 6 binary (polish/judge.toml:20,29,38,47,56,65); scored/visual 3 likert with points = 5 (visual/judge.toml:20-21, 36-37, 52-53). Likert anchors: each of the three visual criteria carries a described anchor at every level 5,4,3,2,1,0 (visual/judge.toml:25-30, 41-46, 57-62), the same shape as the frozen template (template visual/judge.toml:25-33), and visual/prompt.md:7 tells the judge to score with the anchors written in the criterion. The three likert criteria are degree-of-quality asks (editor readability, workspace layout, component finish), which is what likert is for. Binary side: every one of the 48 scored binary criteria and the 3 gate criteria contains an explicit 'Fails if' condition (scripted scan found none without one), and the ones closest to craft are still stated as observable thresholds rather than degrees: syntax colouring demands five visibly different treatments and fails if any two look the same (functional/judge.toml:173); narrow width fails on sideways scrolling or controls that cannot be read or pressed (polish/judge.toml:67); keyboard/focus, feedback, focus return, Undo/Redo availability and unsaved marker are present/absent behaviours (polish/judge.toml:22-58). No craft or degree-of-quality criterion is typed binary and no likert block lacks anchors, so neither failure mode named in SKILL.md:65 and quality-checks.md:170 occurs. The internal workbook annotation (Internal Quality Checks E42: 'we use binary and weighted. Likert we dont use in rewardkit') is the known false positive those two skill passages tell reviewers not to flag; the shipped template itself uses likert in visual. Probes: a plausible broken app with an ugly but working UI loses only graded visual points (not all-or-nothing), and a conforming app with an unusual palette is protected by visual/prompt.md:20 (do not penalise colour choice) and loses no binary credit for taste. Actual-run support on an earlier candidate only (hash bacbf94c... verified): the configured judge returned raw 5 -> 1.0 and raw 4 -> 0.75 for these same likert criteria, visual 0.9167, so likert was accepted and graded by RewardKit; this is not a measurement of the current bytes and is not needed for this static row. Non-blocking observation: that normalisation is (raw-1)/4, so anchors 1 and 0 both yield 0, and the task prompt drops the template's sentences that the 0-5 anchors override RewardKit's generic '1 to 5' hint and that scores are single integers (template visual/prompt.md:36-42 versus task visual/prompt.md:7). Anchors are still described at every level, so this does not fail row 41.
suggested_fix: Optional, not required for this row: restore in tests/scored/visual/prompt.md the template wording that the anchored 0-5 scale is authoritative over RewardKit's generic 1-to-5 hint and that one integer anchor is chosen.
